newsitem.title: CHINA: Nationalist HK politician apologises in freedom row.
newsitem.headline: Nationalist HK politician apologises in freedom row.

text.p: A Hong Kong politician who sparked a row with a whiff of racism over academic freedoms has apologised to two professors but blamed his rudeness on his own American education, a newspaper said on Wednesday.

The pro-China legislator and businessman, David Chu, had attacked sinologist David Baum of the Chinese University of Hong Kong and journalism professor Tim Hamlett of Baptist University as being unfit for the job after they challenged his views.

Hong Kong radio listeners heard Chu and Hamlett, a Briton, wage a fierce slanging match on a live breakfast chat show on Tuesday, when the academic accused Chu of waging a racist campaign to drive foreigners out of the former British colony.
Hamlett later told the South China Morning Post Chu phoned and apologised "at great length and in handsome fashion".
Chu told the paper he would also apologise to American China expert Baum, and admitted: "I was quite rude to him."
But Chu excised himself for his rudeness, saying: "Maybe I picked up some of this in my American education."
At the centre of the row were letters which Chu sent to the professors and their superiors casting the two in a bad light. Hamlett described the letter as "a farrago of racist abuse".
Chu has often written newspaper columns and given speeches with a strong whiff of Chinese nationalism which many have interpreted as anti-foreign.

Chu was educated in the United States but says he has given up his American citizenship. He is campaigning to erase colonial influence from Hong Kong education. China resumed sovereignty over Hong Kong on July 1, ending 156 years of colonial rule.
Hundreds of foreign professors work at the universities in this predominantly Chinese community.
